title: Setting Up SSH Keys for Github Access
author: Ken Youens-Clark
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jh7cj9n

steps.title: Log in and open Settings
steps.instruction: Sign in to your GitHub account, click your profile menu, and select “Settings”.

steps.title: Navigate to SSH Keys
steps.instruction: In Settings, select the “SSH and GPG keys” section on the left (marked as (1)) and click the “New SSH key” button in the upper‑right corner (marked as (2)).

substeps.instruction: Select SSH and GPG keys on left (1)

steps.title: Add new SSH public key
steps.instruction: Copy the contents of your public key file (~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub) from your computer, paste it into the “Key” field, give it a descriptive title such as “laptop” or “UA HPC”, and press the green “Add SSH key” button.

steps.title: Clone repository via SSH
steps.instruction: Clone the desired repository using its SSH URL (e.g., git clone git@github.com:user/repo.git).

steps.title: Convert existing repo to SSH
steps.instruction: If the repository was previously cloned with HTTPS, open the file .git/config in the repository directory and replace the URL that begins with https:// with the corresponding SSH URL (git@github.com:...).

steps.title: Test push/pull without password
steps.instruction: Perform a git push or git pull; it should succeed without prompting for a GitHub password.
